items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: a man by the name of Mason who was the manager of the Academy... naturally, Ike Levy called him and he said yes.

ctx.x: And then...I had bought a club with a couple of guys, an after hours spot. Well, it was a club, you know, drinking and that business. In Philadelphia on Sunday you couldn't buy whiskey. But we had...this is when we had our sessions. So I bought this club with Felix Valdez and some more people and we used to have Jazz Festival Society concerts in the

club. Then I decided, well, what the hell. I went to Ike Levy and asked him to call the Academy of Music and see if they'd let me have the foyer. And a man by the name of Mason who was the manager of the Academy...naturally, Ike Levy called him and he said yes. So then I started having the concerts in the foyer, the foyer of the Academy of Music.

Then I decided that I'd have a big concert. That's when I had Art Tatum and Sidney Bechet. I say that that was the first jazz festival ever held, you know what I mean, in America by a black. And I don't remember anybody else ever having held one before 1947, do you? And then I had Art Tatum, Sidney Bechet, Baby Dodds and Milton Mezzrow and, you know, a lot of people like that.
